request.spec:
A transfer to a sheet that already has a person with the same name or alias (as names are
compared) now merges the arriving person into them instead of being refused, exactly as a merge
does (claims after theirs, aliases joined, bound figures lost); the other sheet writes
PERSON_TRANSFERRED name=<name> from=<sheet id> then PERSON_MERGED from=<name> into=<name>.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A transfer to a sheet that already has a person with the same name or alias (as names are
compared) now merges the arriving person into them instead of being refused, exactly as a merge
does (claims after theirs, aliases joined, bound figures lost); the other sheet writes
PERSON_TRANSFERRED name=<name> from=<sheet id> then PERSON_MERGED from=<name> into=<name>.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
A transfer to a sheet that already has a person with the same name or alias now merges the arriving person into that person instead of being refused. `bin/e2e` passes: all 4 acceptance tests.

**What happens now** (in `person/TransferPerson.java`):
- **Finding the match:** the transfer looks for someone on the other sheet whose name or alias matches the arriving person's name or any of their aliases. Matching ignores case and surrounding spaces, the same way the app already compares names.
- **Moving:** the person and their claims move across exactly as before. Their claims get the other sheet's next numbers and lose any figures a statement bound.
- **Merging:** the app then runs the same steps as a normal merge. Their claims are listed after the existing person's, their name and aliases become that person's aliases, and the person merged in leaves the list.
- **Audit:** the other sheet records `PERSON_TRANSFERRED … name=<name> from=<sheet>`, then `PERSON_MERGED … from=<name> into=<name>`, then its rollup lines. The sending sheet's audit lines are unchanged.

Supporting edits: `Transfer` now records who the person was merged into, `AuditPersonArrived` writes the merge line, and I updated the comment in `transfer.POST.yml`. There were no front-end or schema changes.

**Choices the request didn't spell out** — say if you want any of them different:
- If the arriving person's names match more than one person on the other sheet, the transfer is still refused, because there's no single person to merge into.
- If the matching person is retired, the transfer is refused, since a normal merge refuses retired people too.
- When a merge happens, the contact check is skipped: a merge drops the arriving person's contact, so it doesn't need to be free on the other sheet.
- Name clashes on other sheets in the receiving sheet's tree are still refused, as before.

The test only exercises the single-match merge, so these choices aren't covered by it.
